comparator.name: Industrial Engineering and Management
comparator.sourceNotes: The formally published 2026-2027 programme appendix establishes a complete 180-ECTS pathway: 60 ECTS of compulsory first-year courses; a 30-ECTS common IEM core across Years 2-3; a 40-ECTS specialisation; 30 ECTS of genuine minor space; and the 20-ECTS Bachelor Integration Project. The generic normalized target requires one of two equal 40-ECTS specialisations. Neither is formally presented as more representative, so Production Technology and Logistics is selected by the official-order tie-break. The minor space remains open rather than being populated with invented courses. The current programme page independently describes the degree as two-thirds technical science and one-third business, with training in mathematical and physical modelling, production, logistics, sustainability, management and technical/economic feasibility.

routeSelection.basis: The generic IEM target has two formally named, equal-sized specialisations and current official evidence does not establish either as more representative or general. The first-listed specialisation in the 2026-2027 appendix is therefore selected neutrally, without regard to UCR fit.

programmes.label: Industrial Engineering and Management at University of Groningen

exception.reason: Groningen explicitly defines Industrial Engineering and Management as a predominantly technical engineering degree: two-thirds technical science and one-third business. The selected pathway combines calculus, linear algebra, statistics, programming, materials and transport phenomena with engineering-system dynamics, complex-system design, mechanics, signals, control, CAD and manufacturing, production techniques, construction, mechanical craftsmanship and a 20-ECTS industrial integration project. UCR can reproduce meaningful business, data, programming, mathematics, sustainability and product-design context, but it has no coherent mechanics, materials, transport, manufacturing, control-engineering, construction or workshop sequence and no comparable industrial-engineering capstone. A 24-course UCR programme would therefore shift the degree's centre of gravity from engineering to general business and data study rather than constitute a defensible closest match.
exception.curriculumContext: The formal 2026-2027 pathway totals exactly 180 ECTS: 60 ECTS in Year 1, 30 ECTS of common advanced IEM core, the 40-ECTS Production Technology and Logistics specialisation, 30 ECTS of open minor space and a 20-ECTS Integration Project. The compulsory technical spine progresses from materials, physical transport, modelling and system dynamics to mechanics, signals and systems, control, CAD/manufacturing, production techniques, engineering construction and mechanical craftsmanship. The integration project requires 140 ECTS of prior programme completion.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR workbook, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide relevant quantitative foundations. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science and DISARIN311 Optimization Methods in AI add programming, modelling and optimisation. BENGATE101 Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, BENBUSI112 Accounting & Corporate Finance, BENENTR211 Marketing & Consumer Engagement, BENENTR212 Strategy & Digital Transformation, BENENTR311 Market Research and BENLEAD311 Psychology of Organizations & Leadership provide business and organisational perspectives. BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design offers one team-based product-development and prototyping experience, while ENSSUST112 Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy, ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design add sustainability and technical-economic assessment. The workbook nevertheless contains no engineering mechanics, materials-and-molecules or transport-phenomena course; no manufacturing-process, CAD, workshop or mechanical-craftsmanship sequence; no physical system dynamics and control-engineering laboratory; no industrial production-planning or quality-control sequence; and no 20-ECTS industrial integration project. DISMATH312 studies mathematical linear systems rather than physical engineering-system analysis and control implementation, and BENENTR111 cannot replace a cumulative manufacturing, construction and workshop curriculum.
